WARBL Scala Fingering Lab portable development build. Field operators, bell behavior, and teaching paths remain simulation-first until physical WARBL evidence is recorded.
Start here — browser, launch, MIDI routing, and support

Open the Lab

Double-click the included WSFL HTML file and allow Chrome or another current Chromium-based browser to open it. The complete interface is contained in that one portable file; no server window or platform launcher is required.

Browser MIDI and WARBL permissions remain browser-controlled. Save valuable projects and mappings as exported files rather than relying only on browser storage.

Browser

Use a current Chromium-based desktop browser with Web MIDI enabled. Open the Laboratory as a top-level page, not inside an embedded frame. The connection diagnostic reports browser context, permission, ports, and incoming traffic without changing the WARBL.

DAW / virtual MIDI

Select a virtual MIDI cable or hardware port under Retuned MIDI destination, then choose External Synth / DAW. On Linux, a visible MIDI Through Port-0 is a valid browser-reported MIDI destination. Match the receiving synth's pitch-bend range to the Laboratory.

Support

Email xencanvas@gmail.com for a bug report or feature request. Include the scale file, operating system, browser, Laboratory version, and the copied MIDI diagnostic report when relevant.

Updates

Update checks are manual. When the Laboratory is hosted from its GitHub project, this button reads the project’s small version manifest; it never installs or replaces the Lab automatically.

Known MPE Legato profile

If device readback does not confirm the bend range or legato state, you can explicitly use the MPE Legato ±96 template: channel 3, legato lifecycle, ±96-semitone bend interpretation, Channel Pressure, and CC74 expressive control. Evidence becomes gesture

Phrase Shape / Aperture

The active Scala file now builds the pitch field at the left of the spectrogram. The exact white MPE trajectory remains primary evidence; line thickness follows pressure. Boxed landings show degree, ratio/cents, expressive deviation, and live MPE context. Aperture can then compress several microgestures into a few broad narrative forms without replacing the evidence underneath.

Scala landscape · MPE evidence · narrative
measured MPE trajectory Aperture broad form Scala landing + MPE evidence
The Scala file defines the proportional pitch landscape; MPE performance draws the path.

Evidence rule: Scala lines and MPE values are measured or deterministically derived. The pale broad forms are interpretations: delayed, provisional when necessary, and always recoverable to the source span shown below. Aperture may dream, but every dream must be reversible to evidence.

Ready. Play the internal Reference Instrument or run the short demo.

White trajectory: pitch from actual MPE bend; thickness follows pressure. Boxes: Scala target + deviation + pressure/CC74/channel when present. Broad forms: sparse temporal compression, not event-by-event icons.

Aperture narrative — reversible evidence

Each form is stored as an interpretation of a specific source span. Measured, derived, and interpreted information are kept visibly separate.

    Fingering Grammar & Register Architecture

    The eight sequential states are an ergonomic spine, not an eight-note limit.

    256-state aware

    This build records and explains register architecture. Physical thumb, half-hole, bell, button, and firmware behavior remain device-configuration facts and are not inferred from the Scala file.

    Playable Fields & Pitch Operators

    Reuse one learnable eight-hole grammar across periods, adjacent windows, generators, ratios, and carefully declared alternatives.

    simulation-first

    Verification boundary: these layers are exact software transformations of the active tuning. A declared bell, overblow, button, thumb, or IMU control remains designed or simulated until it is configured, observed, and physically verified.

    Performance Scenes

    bridge-neutral
    No scene has been captured in this session.

    Boundary: the manual buttons emit generic scene messages now. The selected command source and number are stored as capsule metadata for a separate Performance Scene Bridge, foot controller, Stream Deck, DAW cue, or collaborator’s software; this build does not yet bind incoming Program Change, CC, or footswitch messages to scene advancement.     Extended Scale Mapping

    Keep the complete mapping, or explore overlapping fingering systems for learning, notation, and present-day DAW overdubbing.

    optional · multi-system

    How to use multiple systems today

    1. Export each system and place its chart in a separate WARBL custom slot where supported.
    2. Create a separate DAW track and tuning-aware VST instance for each system.
    3. Select the matching WARBL chart, retuned MIDI route, and armed track.
    4. Record or overdub each system in a separate pass, or change systems only at a tested musical boundary.

    Current limitation: the Laboratory does not yet switch a WARBL chart, Scala realization, and VST route atomically during a continuous performance. Automatic switching belongs to the separate WARBL Tuning Bridge / Performance Scene Bridge. Native button-controlled chart switching remains a firmware request and is not claimed here.

    Export and install

    Human-readable rationale and machine-readable mappings share one data model.

    Direct WARBL2 installation

    Writes the validated 256-value chart only after explicit confirmation. Assignment to the active preset is optional and never changes breath, legato, register, pressure, buttons, channel, or bend range.

    Read Current WARBL Setup to see the active preset and current chart.
    Not sent.

    Boundary: direct chart transmission follows the open-source WARBL2 Configuration Tool protocol and requires acknowledgement. Complete 256-value readback from an existing custom slot is not claimed. Exact Scala offsets still require a retuned synth, pitch bend/MPE, MTS, or another tuning-aware destination.

    About & updates — version, update manifest, and release boundary

    Installed build

    WARBL Scala Fingering Lab v1.0.0-rc.1

    Recovery provenance: reconstructed from the preserved 07d05eb9… late integration snapshot and the verified audit.12b baseline after the historical c73bcfce… bytes were not recoverable. Software gates are rerun on this new identity; physical WARBL acceptance remains separate.

    Execution-path refinement: recovered.2 moves diagnostic formatting, Phrase Shape enrichment, lifecycle witnesses, breath presentation, MPE monitor painting, and dormant test taps away from the realtime audio/MIDI handoff while preserving musical authority and output semantics.

    Handoff refinement: recovered.3 makes TP11 contiguous with the actual reference-output call in normal performance and gives final reference-note release priority over observer/practice work.

    Cumulative realtime refinement: recovered.4 keeps Flight Recorder hot retention shallow, gives external releases and raw-fingering corrections priority over semantic witnesses, removes repeated full WARBL/MPE/Pattern panel reconstruction from live expression, and defers dense WARBL configuration/sensor presentation while preserving device-state authority.

    Recorder refinement: recovered.5 retains the recovered.4 cumulative execution repairs while allocating hot retained-evidence copies only when the early/critical evidence ledgers actually need them.

    Physical-workflow correction: recovered.6 keeps every recovered.5 execution-path repair, makes Lab Fingering the normal performance authority, makes Connect idempotent and starts Live Sensors when possible, auto-pauses/resumes sensors around setup reads, gives Pitch Geometry an independent physical-input witness, reports exact block reasons, replaces idle failure language with ready/standby states, and turns the Notation rendering boundary into a non-interactive instruction callout.

    Physical-trace correction: recovered.7 keeps recovered.6 authority and UI behavior, makes Lab-fingering pitch bend obey the same per-fingering local anchor during continuous expression and raw-sensor reconciliation, adds a reference-frequency consistency repair after fresh hole state, yields during Project Export ZIP assembly, establishes a deliberate print/non-realtime boundary that discards stale queued MIDI, and records the actual interactive control behind pointer events for future stall attribution.

    Control + raw-state correction: recovered.8 preserves recovered.7 musical behavior, wires the two Extended Scale Mapping controls, repairs Pattern Tutor / Practice structural signatures, reacquires current raw WARBL state after blocking browser UI, and reduces stale-fingering attack transients by committing paired WARBL hole bytes immediately plus a short conditional raw-sync only inside a recent transition window.

    v1.0 RC precision gate: exact Scala cents remain floating-point source truth through internal frequency realization; release simulation includes the supplied FirstideaTarsos close pair (852.5373134328358¢ / 855.223880597015¢) plus 1.0¢, 0.5¢, and 0.1¢ internal distinction witnesses. External MIDI/MPE precision remains destination- and bend-range-dependent.

    This build as a whole is software-verified and awaits physical WARBL / external receiver acceptance. Individual subsystems may retain separately recorded user-observed or physical-trace evidence from earlier accepted builds.

    Check for updates

    The Lab never silently updates itself. A hosted GitHub copy can read WARBL_LATEST.json from the same project location and offer the release page when a newer build exists.
